summary: Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist who studied at St Beuno's Jesuit Spirituality Centre and Humboldt University of Berlin (Promotion, 1908–1913). He served as Professor of Sanskrit and ancient Indian philosophy at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930) and headed the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Robin Coningham is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at King's College and the University of Cambridge under Frank Raymond Allchin (PhD, ~1989–1994). He held posts at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (2005).

Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar in sinology and archaeology who completed his PhD at Harvard University (~1975–1980). Around 1990, he was appointed to a James McGill Professorship at McGill University.

Robin Dunbar studied at Magdalen College School and Magdalen College, later completing doctoral research under John Crook (~1969–1974). He held a post at University College London from around 1987 to 1994.

Roderick M. Chisholm was a philosopher who studied at Brown University and Harvard University (PhD, ~1938–1942). He taught at the Barnes Foundation, Brown University (~1947–1999), and the University of Graz, and served as president of the Metaphysical Society of America.

Roderick S. Bucknell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Queensland, where he served starting around 1976 and later as Associate Professor from around 1995 to 2002.

Roger Brown was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who completed his studies at the University of Michigan between ~1945 and 1952. He subsequently held a long-term academic post at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.
Roger Heim studied at École Centrale Paris (~1920–1923) and the Science Faculty of Paris (until 1931). He held a post at the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle from around 1929 to 1970.

Roger R. Jackson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Wesleyan University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Carleton College from ~1989 to 2016.

Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and sinologist who studied at UBC, NTU, CUHK, and SOAS under D. C. Lau (PhD, 1975–1978). He held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1978–2016) and Peking University (~2016).

Roland Barthes was a philosopher and linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the CNRS (~1953–1959), EHESS (~1962–1976), and the Collège de France (1976–1980).
Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn. He is attested as an assistant professor at the University of Marburg in 2002.

Roland Wenzlhuemer is a historian who earned his doctorate at the University of Salzburg and completed his habilitation at Heidelberg University. He held positions at Heidelberg, the University of Basel, and became Professor of Modern History at the University of Munich in 2017.

Rolf A. Stein was a Tibetologist and sinologist who studied under Paul Pelliot, Marcel Granet, and others. He served as directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1951–1975) and professor at the Collège de France (1965–1982).

Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna under Helmut Tauscher and also studied under the traditional teacher Khenpo Chödrag Tenphel.

Romila Thapar is a historian and Indologist who studied at Panjab University and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. She was a professor of ancient Indian history at the University of Delhi and Jawaharlal Nehru University.
Ron Garry is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Lama Tharchin Rinpoche as a traditional teacher and under Tulku Thubten Rinpoche.
Ron Leifer was a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. He studied under Agehananda Bharati in 1964 and under the traditional teacher Khenpo Karthar Rinpoche.

Ronald D. Schwartz is a scholar in Tibetology and sociology. In 1998, he was attested as Professor of Sociology at Memorial University of Newfoundland and as an Honorary Research Fellow at The University of Hong Kong.

Ronald E. Purser is a scholar in religious studies and philosophy who studied under Koshin Ogui in 1985. He held posts at Loyola University Chicago (~1991–1997) and San Francisco State University (~1997) as Professor of Management.
